name: Laws of the Resurrection

sources: Mind's Eye Theatre: Laws of the Resurrection (WW05035), "Weapon Examples"/Armor chapter, pp.193-198 - every entry checked against the accumulated catalog so far (Dark Epics, Laws of the Night Revised Edition, Laws of the Hunt, Laws of the East, Laws of the Reckoning); a same-name entry whose stats match an already-catalogued one is left out of this file.
Every entry read directly from the book's own page images (not OCR), per reference-wod-scan-ocr-lessons. This copy's own printed page numbers are plain, legible Arabic numerals.

notes: This book's own weapon-chapter text is independently written throughout, not copied from the other MET corebooks the way most of them copy from each other - most of its entries still land on identical stats regardless, and only 5 of roughly 20 printed carry a real difference.

Spear here prints no Special Ability at all, where Laws of the Reckoning's own Spear explicitly grants Staking - a real loss of capability, not an omission to fill in, so it's kept as its own entry rather than assumed to carry Staking anyway.

Longbow's own Armor-Piercing text here covers chain armor and ballistic vests - wider than any other printing's chain-armor-only wording - and prints no Staking at all, where every other printing grants it.

items.name: Knife/Dagger
items.description: Characters with the Athletics Ability can throw knives/daggers as well as use them in hand-to-hand combat.

availability.name: Any martial arts store, though spears cost much more than staves and it's near impossible to justify carrying spears in policed areas

items.name: Shortsword

availability.name: Any. Blade strength counts for less with shortswords than with broadswords, and even replicas can deliver one or a few useful blows if sharpened

items.description: Covers all blades up to about 18 inches long, designed primarily for thrusting - the gladius, scuta, jiann and similar weapons.

properties.concealability: Trenchcoat (with -1 Trait penalty to concealment challenges)

availability.name: Must usually be special-ordered, though cheap and unreliable ones can be found at military supply stores and Renaissance festivals. At the Storyteller's discretion, they suffer from the Negative Trait of Fragile, as well as the standard Heavy

items.name: Longbow

properties.powers: Armor-Piercing (ignores chain armor and ballistic vests), Destroy Shield

items.description: Use the Athletics Ability for retests when using bows; characters who lack Athletics receive only one third of the usual Bonus Traits, rounded down. Modern compound bows do not have the Negative Trait of Clumsy, but give only five Bonus Traits.
